reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus is the largest data center in Illinois with a disclosed power figure, and it alone accounts for 48 percent of the state's published IT capacity.

The campus publishes 114 megawatts of IT capacity across three buildings and 450,000 square feet, which works out to about 6.3 megawatts per 10,000 square feet. That ratio is ordinary for hyperscale colocation built in the last decade, so the site's distinction is its size, not its density. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 114 megawatts supports roughly 2,850 racks.

The number matters because disclosed capacity is rare. Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities and only six with published power figures, so a single campus holding nearly half the state's disclosed total shows how much of the state's actual load is invisible in the public record. Power is the binding constraint on AI scaling, and the public record captures only a fraction of it.

What the data does not cover is decisive. There is no published figure for total campus draw, PUE, renewable sourcing, grid connection characteristics, or cloud interconnect. Whether this campus can actually host modern accelerator clusters depends on whether the local grid constrains its power budget and whether its cooling handles that thermal density, and neither is disclosed. The 114 megawatts is a nameplate figure, not evidence of available headroom.
